title: Is This a Good Place for Active Management? | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional argues that small caps and non-US stocks, despite thinner analyst coverage, are not fertile ground for stock pickers: over the 20 years to September 30, 2026 only a minority of funds in US small cap, non-US developed small cap and emerging markets survived and outperformed. It suggests a flexible, systematic active approach rather than stock picking, given higher trading costs in these segments.

themes.theme: Fewer analysts does not mean easier stock picking

insights.claim: The popular belief that small caps and non-US stocks are more amenable to stock picking rests on thin analyst coverage implying weaker price information, but Dimensional argues the aggregate record of stock pickers in these markets has not been impressive.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Challenges the 'inefficient corner' justification for paying active fees in small-cap and international allocations.
insights.quote: While it may be true there are fewer analysts, I think we can safely say that in aggregate the performance of stock pickers in these markets has not been impressive.

insights.claim: Fewer analysts covering a stock is treated as an insufficient condition for active outperformance: the perceived information gap does not translate into realized aggregate manager alpha.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Low coverage alone should not be accepted as evidence of exploitable mispricing when selecting managers.

themes.theme: Evidence: survivorship and outperformance over 20 years

insights.claim: Dimensional uses the aggregate performance of non-indexed funds as the proxy for the efficacy of active management, applied the same way as in the prior week's piece.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Method is a whole-universe, survivorship-aware hit rate rather than selected-manager track records.
insights.quote: our proxy for the efficacy of active management is the aggregate performance of non-indexed funds

insights.claim: Across US small cap, non-US developed small cap and emerging market stocks, only a minority of the funds available at the start of the 20-year period to September 30, 2026 both survived and outperformed their benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Odds of picking a fund that both survives and beats its benchmark in these segments are below even over two decades; exact percentages are in Exhibit 1, not in the text.
insights.quote: only a minority of the funds that were available at the start of the 20-year period survived and outperformed

themes.theme: Cost drag in thinly traded markets

insights.claim: Trading costs tend to be even higher for small caps and non-US stocks, which raises the hurdle for active managers and weakens the case for simply buying the market index in these categories too.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Implementation cost, not just selection skill, drives net outcomes in less liquid segments.
insights.quote: the costs of trading tend to be even higher for small caps and non-US stocks

themes.theme: Systematic active as the proposed middle path

insights.claim: Rejecting stock picking does not mean settling for pure indexing in these segments: an active approach that uses flexibility to deliver systematic equity exposure may give more reliable outcomes than trying to pick stocks in thinly traded markets.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Positions Dimensional's flexible, systematic implementation as the answer; the piece is advocacy by a manager selling that approach, so treat the claim with that bias in mind.
insights.quote: An active approach that uses flexibility to provide systematic equity exposure, rather than spinning its wheels trying to pick stocks, may give investors more reliable outcomes in these markets that can be more thinly traded.

insights.claim: The piece is a short follow-up to a prior entry on whether it is time for active management to shine, and carries related pieces titled 'Is This a Good Time for Active Management?', 'Double Trouble' and 'Can You Handle the Tracking Error?'.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Indicates a Dimensional content series on the active-versus-passive debate at the end of October 2026.

source_meta.author: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
